newsitem.title: CHINA: China port sees little impact from tanker fire.
newsitem.headline: China port sees little impact from tanker fire.

text.p: China's eastern port of Nanjing will see little impact from an explosion that sank an oil tanker and a barge this week, harbour officials said on Friday.
The explosion of the Daqing 243 tanker on Wednesday at the Qixia anchorage on the Yangtze River had shut down an area with a capacity for four vessels, mainly used for unloading oil.
But other anchorages were vacant and would be used to offset the impact.
The explosion while the tanker was unloading crude oil did not affect shipping lanes and there would be no disruption of ship traffic, officials said.
They added that the pollution threat had been brought under control but declined to give further details.

Officials had said earlier the Daqing 243 tanker of the Guangzhou Ocean Shipping Group had been carrying 19,464 tonnes of crude oil. About 6,000 tonnes of crude were still aboard the vessel at the time of the blast.
Eight people are listed as missing in the blast.
